message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*  
> *You must have a project with billing enabled, the **Compute Engine API** turned on, and the **GPU API** enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` and `gcloud services enable cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com`).*  
> *You also need to have the NVIDIA driver installed on the instance (the image we use below already contains the driver).*

---

## 1.  `gcloud` CLI command

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU (type `nvidia-a6000`, count 1) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image that already contains the NVIDIA driver |
| `--boot-disk-size` | 100 GB SSD for OS + data |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script on first boot (e.g., to install extra packages) |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the instance running during zone maintenance |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, just change `GPU_COUNT` (max 8 per instance for RTX A6000).

---

## 2.  REST API (curl)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal `curl` example that creates the same instance.  
(Replace placeholders with your own values.)

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' PAYLOAD <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  },
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$PAYLOAD"
```

### Explanation of the JSON

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image, 100 GB SSD) |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Uses the default VPC with external IP |
| `scheduling` | Keeps the instance alive during maintenance and restarts on failure |

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **Enable APIs**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   gcloud services enable cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Create a GPU‑enabled zone** (if not already available).  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute zones list | grep us-central1-a | grep "GPU"
   ```

3. **Create the instance** using either the `gcloud` command or the REST API.

4. **Verify** that the instance shows up in the console and that the GPU is visible:  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --command "nvidia-smi"
   ```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
